safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(والضحى) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم ("I swear") (إذا) is an adverbial in the position of accusative, stripped of the conditional sense, attached to the verb أقسم (ما) is negating in both places..
Clause: « (أقسم) بالضحى ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
And the clause: «سجي ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ما ودّعك ربّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the jawāb al-qasam.
And the clause: «ما قلى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(2) سجي: it contains an ʿilāl by substitution; its origin is سجو — its imperfect is يسجو — meaning "became still", of the bāb of نصر. The wāw, vowelled after a fatḥa, was changed to alif. By right it should have been written with the long alif (سجا), but the orthography of the muṣḥaf came with the undotted yāʾ (سجي) to suit the reading with imāla..
(3) قلى: it contains an ʿilāl by substitution; its origin is قلو — its imperfect is يقلو — of the bāb of نصر. The wāw, vowelled after a fatḥa, was changed to alif, and the reason for writing it with the short alif is the same as for سجي..
It is stated in al-Miṣbāḥ: قليت الرجل أقليه, of the bāb of ضرب, when you hate him, and of the bāb of تعب as a dialectal form; so the alif is both from wāw and from yāʾ at once.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His saying, the Exalted «وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا سَجى».
That is, its people became still, taking it from سجو, which is stillness in general. The attribution is figurative, since stillness is attributed to the night while it belongs to its people.

* Benefits:
- The occasion of revelation of the sūra:
The scholars differed on the occasion of revelation of this sūra, in three views:
1-
On the authority of Jundub ibn Sufyān al-Bajalī, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill and did not rise for two or three nights. A woman came and said: "O Muhammad, I hope that your devil has left you; I have not seen him near you for two or three nights." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed (والضحى والليل إذا سجي). Al-Tirmidhī also transmitted it from Jundub, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave, and his finger bled, so the Prophet ﷺ said:
هل أنت إلا إصبع دميت ... وفي سبيل الله ما لقيت
(You are but a finger that bled; and in the path of Allah is what you have met.)
He said: Then Gabriel was slow in coming to him, and the polytheists said: "Muhammad has been abandoned." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed (ما وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَما قَلى).
It is also said that the woman mentioned in the agreed-upon hadith is Umm Jamīl, the wife of Abū Lahab.
2-
The commentators said: The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the spirit, about Dhū l-Qarnayn and the companions of the cave, and he said: "I shall tell you tomorrow," and did not say "if Allah wills", so the revelation was withheld from him, and then it came down.
3-
Zayd ibn Aslam said: The reason the revelation was withheld was that a puppy was in his house, and when he [Translator's note: i.e. Gabriel] came down the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reproached him for his delay, and he said: "We do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image."
They also differed on the length of time the revelation was withheld from him; it is said: twelve days. It is evident that the first report is the strongest regarding the occasion of revelation, and it agrees more with the facts.

safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction (اللام) is the lām of oath in both places (لك) is attached to (خير), (من الأولى) is attached to (خير)..
Clause: «للآخرة خير ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the preceding answer to the oath [Note: in verse (3) of the sūra; and the lām is brought because the statement is affirmative after a negative.].
And the clause: «سوف يعطيك ربّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the preceding answer to the oath; and the clause: «ترضى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يعطيك.

safi-cedvel:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr) (يتيما) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الفاء) is a conjunction in the three places, and the object of (آوى) is implied, and likewise the two objects of (هدى, أغنى) ...
Clause: «لم يجدك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «آوى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «وجدك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «هدى» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause وجدك.
And the clause: «وجدك (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «أغنى» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause وجدك (the second).

* Morphology:
(8) عائلا: an active participle from عال يعيل, of the bāb of ضرب, its pattern is فاعل, and it contains the change of the weak letter into a hamza after the alif of فاعل; its origin is عايل, i.e. poor..

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (al-isti'āra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, the Exalted «وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدى».
Here the sharia is likened to guidance (hudā), and its not being found to straying (ḍalāl); the thing likened was dropped and the thing likened to was kept, namely straying.

safi-cedvel:9-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is the connecting particle of the jawāb of an implied condition (أمّا) is a particle of condition and elaboration (اليتيم) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi, its governing verb being (تقهر), (الفاء) is the connecting particle of the jawāb of أمّا (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle (الواو) is a conjunction in both places (أمّا السائل فلا تنهر) is like أمّا اليتيم فلا تقهر, (بنعمة) is attached to (حدّث), and the fāʾ does not prevent that [Note: because the fāʾ is in the ruling of a redundant one, or because it is later in order than what was fronted.]..
Clause: «جملة الشرط أمّا وجوابه» has no grammatical position; it is the jawāb of an implied condition, i.e. "if your state was thus — orphanhood, straying and poverty — then whatever the case may be, do not oppress the orphan ..."
And the two following clauses of condition with their answers are conjoined to the first clause.
And the clause: «تقهر ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing condition.
And the clause: «تنهر ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing condition.
And the clause: «حدّث ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing condition.

* Benefits:
Kindness to the orphan and the beggar:
In these two verses is lofty guidance and noble character: they urge the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to treat the orphan gently and not to rebuke the beggar. This address is not to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone, but to every believer.
Al-Baghawī reported with his chain, from Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The best house among the Muslims is a house in which there is an orphan who is treated well, and the worst house among the Muslims is a house in which there is an orphan who is treated badly." Then he said: "I and the guardian of the orphan will be in Paradise like this," pointing with his two fingers.
And on the authority of Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I and the guardian of the orphan will be in Paradise like this," and he pointed with the index and middle fingers and separated them a little.
As for not rebuking the beggar, the highest meanings of humanity are realized in it. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: "The beggar wants us for the Hereafter; he comes to the door of one of you and says: 'Will you send something with me to your family?'" It is also said: the beggar is the seeker of knowledge, so he must be honoured and helped to what he seeks, not frowned at, not rebuked, and not met with something disliked. In any case, the beggar, whatever kind his request is, whether he asks for money or any need, or asks that you direct him to a place, then either you grant him his request if possible, or else a kind word and an apology.
